question: Q-003
reason: The criterion is satisfied as it stands; I checked it in a browser, not from the files alone. With axe-core 4.14.0 in Chromium and the assert_accessible body of task 9.1, a page with lang and a title holding a labelled button returns, and the same page holding a button without a name fails with "accessibility violations: button-name (critical): button", a message that holds button-name. A bare set_content page with no lang and no title fails both cases with document-title and html-has-lang (serious), which is why the journey tests wrap the button in a minimal document (Q-001). The tracing test checks only that the second case fails, not that its message holds button-name; that is a weak test, not a missing behaviour, and is left for a tests feedback after the merge rather than a fix unit whose red test could not fail.

question: Q-004
reason: The finding is correct. The Dismiss button in ToastRegion carries the class ui-button, and theme.css gives .ui-button:hover (specificity 0,2,0) a background of var(--ui-color-bg), which tokens.css sets to #ffffff. The rule .ui-toast button (specificity 0,1,1) sets the colour to var(--ui-color-toast-text), also #ffffff, and its transparent background loses to the hover rule. So while the pointer hovers the Dismiss button of a toast, its label is white on white, which contradicts the requirement that the theme meets WCAG AA contrast and defeats the toast-text-on-toast-bg pair of design decision 3. axe does not evaluate hover states, so no gate catches it, and this is a real accessibility defect that a user of the toast will meet on every dismissal. The fix belongs in theme.css only, with colours still taken from var(--ui-color-*) tokens so that findRawColours stays empty.
